reference: Innocentius III, Regest. lib. XVI, bull XXVIII, Migne PL 216, cols. 818-820 (Quia maior, 1213)
gist_en: Calls the faithful to take the cross and fight for the Holy Land, invoking Christ's cross and promising remission of sins to crusaders and their financers.
why_excluded: Crusade exhortation (call to war), exclusion rule.

reference: Innocentius III, Regest. lib. XVI, bull XXVIII, Migne PL 216, col. 819-820 (Quia maior, 1213)
gist_en: Threatens excommunication and loss of goods for those who sell arms, iron and timber to the Saracens or serve their ships; cites the Lateran Council sentence.
why_excluded: Economic war measure and sanction; not doctrinal. Refers to Fourth Lateran Council (1215) decree, text not read by me.

reference: Innocentius III, Regest. lib. XVI, bull XXVIII, Migne PL 216, col. 818 (Quia maior, 1213): the Saracen seizure of Mount Tabor and the threat to Acre
gist_en: Narrates recent Saracen fortification on Mount Thabor and threat to Acre, used to urge a military expedition.
why_excluded: War narrative used as call to arms; no doctrinal point about Islam.

reference: Fourth Lateran Council (1215), canons on Saracens (c. 68 dress; c. 71 trade in arms/ships to Saracens) as cited in Quia maior
gist_en: Canons restricting dress distinctions for Jews and Saracens and trade in arms and ships with Saracens (as described in the bull; canon texts not read by me).
why_excluded: Not read in a public-domain text; discriminatory and war/trade measures, not doctrinal. Listed for the orchestrator to know they exist.

reference: Pius II, Epistola ad Mahumetem, PDF page 82 of ita-bnc-in2-00000500-001 (sentence beginning 'Audiamus eum: non sum missus inquit nisi in virtute gladii')
gist_en: Pius quotes Muhammad as saying he was sent only with the power of the sword, and that whoever refuses his prophecy is to be killed or pay tribute for unbelief.
why_excluded: Point concerns violence and war (sword, killing, tribute); exclusion rule. Quoting it would be a call-to-kill or war-claim passage; not put in passages.json.

reference: Pius II, Epistola ad Mahumetem, PDF page 70 of ita-bnc-in2-00000500-001 (sentences on ne quispiam de sua lege disputaret ... ferro vindicandum esse)
gist_en: Pius says Muhammad forbade anyone to dispute his law and ordered that anyone opposing it be avenged with iron (sword).
why_excluded: Point concerns forcible suppression by arms; close to a war/violence statement. Orchestrator should decide; not quoted in passages.json.

reference: Pius II, Epistola ad Mahumetem, PDF page 70 (sentence 'ea praecipiens quae grata essent auditoribus et maxime plebibus que iumentis similes existunt')
gist_en: Pius says Muhammad commanded what pleased hearers, and especially the common folk, who he says are like beasts of burden.
why_excluded: Ethnic/personal insult against people (comparison of the common people to beasts). Not quoted; the non-insulting continuation is in passages.json.
